newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds look to wages to steer the trend.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds look to wages to steer the trend.

text.p: *Australian bond yields crept higher again in early trading, partially reflecting weakness in U.S. Treasuries, and also amid caution ahead of the final first quarter wages report.
*Wages, Q1 company profits due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT)

Australian bond yields crept higher again in early trading, partially reflecting weakness in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday, and also amid caution ahead of the first quarter final average weekly wages report.

Wages growth remains the key issue for the market following recent comments by the Reserve Bank and today's data could rekindle hopes of a further monetary policy easing, or strike such ideas completely off the agenda.
"If we get a high private figure, I suspect the short end will break down pretty badly," one trader said.
Final average weekly ordinary time earnings are due for release and, unlike the preliminary data released earlier this month, they include the private-public sector split.

The market is looking for a private wages outcome below 1.0 percent on the quarter and any downward revision to the overall preliminary data, which came in at 1.3 percent and 4.6 percent year-on-year, to keep slim hopes of an easing alive, analysts said.
RBA governor Ian Macfarlane has repeatedly expressed concerns in recent weeks over wages given that annual growth is running above 4.5 percent and its so-called 'line in the sand'.
Also due at 11.30 a.m., but somewhat overshadowed by the wages data, will be first quarter company profits.
Forecasts centre on a 2.0 percent fall after the 8.6 percent jump in the December quarter, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

The long end of the U.S. Treasury curve weakened on Wednesday amid hedge fund selling and supply concerns, combined with a sharp 19.2 percent drop in the March U.S. trade gap, which suggested that the economy continued to grow.
The U.S. short end remain buoyed by the Federal Reserve's decision to leave policy on hold on Tuesday.

The local market again underperformed against Canada, which continued to benefit from the Fed's stable policy stance and pushed the 30-year yield spread to the U.S. to a new low of just three basis points on Wednesday.
